# Pass 4 — Batch E: Canonical AI-System Architecture Decision

## Decision

This batch adopts a standards-derived terminology and evidence architecture for
the current Caelestis corpus. It is an implementation decision, not a claim of
external certification, conformity assessment, or legal compliance.

The principal governed technical object is the **AI system**. An AI model is a
system element; it is not, without further evidence, the whole AI system.

## Source-authority allocation

| Function | Owner | Authority boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Technical system-boundary terminology | `CAM-BS2025-AEON-003-PLATINUM` (Annex B) | Constitutional definitions and non-collapse rules only |
| Runtime applicability, evidence proportionality and conformance operation | `CAM-EQ2026-OPERATIONS-007-PLATINUM` | Derived operational implementation only |
| Constitutional non-presumption of equivalence | Annex B and OPERATIONS-007 | The former Schedule 5 candidate is in the Drafts boundary and has no operative authority |
| Security doctrine | `CAM-EQ2026-SECURITY-001-PLATINUM` | Unchanged by this batch |
| Incident response, evidence custody and containment procedure | `CAM-EQ2026-OPERATIONS-003-PLATINUM` | Unchanged by this batch |
| Contested scope and authority | ARBITRATION instruments | Unchanged by this batch |

No instrument in this batch gains authority to release a hold, authorise an
intervention, create an exception, or resolve a contested authority question.

## Canonical object model

`AI model` → `system element` → `AI system` → `system configuration baseline`
→ `AI system deployment` → `runtime configuration snapshot` → `execution`
→ `execution provenance record`.

The AI-BOM records composition and dependency information. It does not prove
that a declared item participated in a particular execution. Participation is
established, where required and available, by the runtime configuration
snapshot and execution provenance record.

## Terminology disposition

| Retired current term | Replacement is selected by referent |
|---|---|
| Responding Intelligence | AI model, AI agent, AI system, system element, or execution pathway |
| Responding Component | system element or AI component |
| Responding Formation / runtime formation | configuration baseline, deployment, runtime configuration snapshot, or execution provenance record |
| agentic harness | agent orchestration component, agent framework, agent runtime, and configuration |
| governance stack | technical, operational, and organisational governance controls |
| deployed cognitive system | AI system deployment |

`Runtime` remains a defined governance domain. It describes the effective
operational state of an AI-system deployment during execution and is distinct
from both deployment and execution.

## Evidence posture

AI-BOM facts and related evidence use: `declared`, `observed`, `verified`, or
`unknown / undisclosed`. `Declared` is never evidence that a component was
effective in a given execution.

## Deliberate exclusions

This batch does not amend the Four Laws, reopen consciousness/personhood
research, create a competing BOM format, or perform a blind repository-wide
replacement. Historical terminology remains resolvable in prior versions,
amendment ledgers and migration records only.

## Consequential migration

The remaining operative occurrences are a controlled Batch F migration. Each
occurrence must be classified by referent before amendment; terms such as
"identity formation" and ordinary non-technical uses of "formation" are not
technical architecture aliases and must not be mechanically rewritten.
